reasoning: Detector reported that the EMA PRAC index changed from the July 6-9 agenda to the draft October 26-29 agenda (EMA/PRAC/227255/2026). Independent official EMA PDF read confirms its publication date and four-day meeting schedule.

Draft agenda section 3.1.1 lists a newly triggered non-urgent Article 31 benefit-risk referral concerning melitracen hydrochloride and flupentixol hydrochloride (EMA/REF/0000382942), notified by Belgium; it proposes rapporteur appointment and procedural adoption, not a final benefit-risk finding.

Draft agenda section 4.1.1 lists a new human normal immunoglobulin signal of batch-associated hypersensitivity reactions (EPITT 20318) and an item for adoption of a PRAC recommendation; the agenda does not disclose a final adopted recommendation or establish product-level causality.

EMA expressly says this is a working agenda, scopes may change and further details will appear in PRAC meeting highlights when procedures are finalised. The page delta therefore is substantive regulatory-process information but not itself an implemented safety instruction, withdrawal, or clinical advice.

No independent source in this review establishes an adopted October 26-29 PRAC recommendation or new patient-facing guidance. Do not infer medication harm, change treatment, or contact patients from the draft agenda.
action: Preserve as a source-verified pending regulatory signal. No external outreach or clinical claim. Recheck official EMA PRAC meeting highlights or adopted recommendations after the October 29 meeting; only then evaluate whether a material public guidance change warrants a case.

tenthMan.question: If this classification wins, who loses?
tenthMan.risk: Treating a draft agenda as merely routine might delay attention to a real emerging safety signal; treating it as final advice could mislead patients and clinicians.
tenthMan.mitigation: Retain exact identifiers EPITT 20318 and EMA/REF/0000382942, review adopted official outcomes promptly after the meeting, and distinguish signal investigation from regulatory decision.

nextReview: 2026-10-30 or the first publication of official PRAC 26-29 October meeting highlights, whichever is later; otherwise next weekly safety-delta review
closureCondition: Close as triaged when the adopted outcome is reviewed, or when EMA confirms no public-facing action; re-open only on independently verified substantive guidance change.
